title: "DATA 606 Data Project Proposal"
author: "Esra Dogan"

### Data Preparation

```{r setup, echo=TRUE, results='hide', warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

ess <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/esradogan3/final_project_606/refs/heads/main/ess11_widowed_65plus.csv")

widowed <- ess |>
  filter(agea >= 65, agea < 999,    # 999 = age not available
         maritalb == 5,             # 5 = widowed
         fltlnl %in% 1:4,           # remove "refused" / "don't know"
         gndr %in% 1:2) |>
  mutate(
    gender  = factor(gndr, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Men", "Women")),
    lonely  = factor(fltlnl, levels = 1:4,
                     labels = c("None or almost none of the time",
                                "Some of the time",
                                "Most of the time",
                                "All or almost all of the time"))
  )
```

### Research question

**Among widowed adults aged 65 and older, do men feel lonely more often than women?**

- In my current job, I am in contact with many customers, and some of them are people who have lost their spouses. Over time, I noticed that some of them seem much lonelier than others, and I started to wonder whether there might be a difference between widowed men and women. I am 26 and my life experience is limited, so I wanted to see, purely out of curiosity, whether this observation holds up in real data.

### Cases

- Each case is one widowed person aged 65 or older who answered the loneliness question in the European Social Survey.
- There are `r nrow(widowed)` cases (`r sum(widowed$gender == "Men")` men and `r sum(widowed$gender == "Women")` women) from `r n_distinct(widowed$cntry)` countries.

### Data collection

- The European Social Survey (ESS) is a cross-national survey carried out every two years through face-to-face interviews with randomly selected people aged 15 and over.
- I use Round 11 (fieldwork 2023–2024). The data was downloaded as a CSV file from the ESS Data Portal after free registration.

### Type of study

- This is an observational study. People were surveyed, not assigned to groups, so I can describe whether loneliness differs between widowed men and women, but not why.

### Data Source

- European Social Survey European Research Infrastructure (ESS ERIC). (2024). *ESS11 – integrated file, edition 4.2* [Data set]. Sikt – Norwegian Agency for Shared Services in Education and Research. <https://ess.sikt.no/>

### Describe your variables

- **Response variable:** how often the person felt lonely in the past week (`fltlnl`). Categorical (ordinal) with four levels, from "none or almost none of the time" to "all or almost all of the time".
- **Explanatory variable:** gender (`gndr`). Categorical: men or women.
- Variables used for filtering: age (`agea`) and marital status (`maritalb`).

### Relevant summary statistics

Percentage within each gender:

```{r}
widowed |>
  count(gender, lonely) |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = lonely, values_from = percent)
```

Age of the respondents:

```{r}
widowed |>
  group_by(gender) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_age = round(mean(agea), 1), median_age = median(agea))
```

### Planned analysis and limitations

- In the final project, I will use a **chi-square test of independence** to test whether loneliness and gender are related.
- Women make up most of the sample, because women usually live longer and are more often widowed. Using percentages within each gender makes the two groups comparable.
- The ESS provides survey weights so that results represent each country's population. For this proposal I use unweighted data; I will consider the weights in the final project.
